page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is a compute- and memory-intensive virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores (2 threads per core), alongside an exceptionally large memory allocation of 1344.0 GB of RAM. This provides a very high memory density of 84.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and supports instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, driven by high core clock speeds. In Geekbench testing, the server achieved a top-tier single-core score of 2364.0 and a top-tier text processing result of 2950.0. Memory write bandwidth for large uncached blocks reached 91.25 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%. Single-threaded compression workloads also performed well, recording 34.83 GB/sec in gzip and 14.28 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. In contrast, aggregate multi-core tests such as the PassMark CPU score (29523.11) and stress-ng multi-core fall into the median range, constrained by the 16-vCPU count relative to full-socket systems.

A key architectural consideration is the server's resource asymmetry. It provides an exceptionally large pool of RAM while restricting the compute allocation to 16 vCPUs. This configuration optimizes core-licensing costs for workloads that require massive in-memory footprints without needing high parallelism. However, the instance includes no local storage (listed as None) and no GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block storage attachments for stateful tasks.

The Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is well matched for memory-constrained workloads where software licensing is billed per core, such as enterprise in-memory databases (SAP HANA, large Redis deployments, or relational databases), large-scale data caches, and electronic design automation (EDA) tooling.
description: Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is a specialized virtual machine pairing high clock frequency with high memory capacity. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, it features 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 260 MB of L3 cache, and 1344.0 GB of RAM (84.0 GB per core). It includes advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, but provides no integrated local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results highlight top-tier single-core execution (2364.0 in Geekbench) and strong large-block memory write throughput (91.25 GB/sec), while overall multi-core throughput remains moderate due to the 16-thread profile. This resource structure delivers high cost efficiency for software environments licensed per core that demand massive working memory, making it well suited for large in-memory databases, memory-bound caching systems, and electronic design automation workloads.
